mainTopic: Eggs and baby birds: what is forbidden by the Torah and what only by the רבנן, eggs with blood spots, and the source for the איסור of a non-kosher bird's egg.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question from before. A פסוק seemed to forbid chicks whose eyes have not opened, and the גמרא answers that this איסור is only מדרבנן, with the פסוק used as an אסמכתא. Next comes a ברייתא about eggs: boiled eggs, unfertilized eggs, and an egg with a drop of blood. רבי ירמיה and דוסתאי limit the blood-spot leniency: blood on the white is removed and the rest is eaten, but blood on the yolk forbids the whole egg because the decay has spread. רב גביהה reports that אביי fixed a version of this teaching that had it backwards. Then חזקיה derives from the words בת היענה that a non-kosher bird's egg is forbidden מן התורה. The גמרא asks whether בת היענה is simply the bird's name and tests this against פסוקים in איכה, מיכה and ישעיהו. It ends up admitting that both יענה and בת יענה are names of the bird. The amud closes as the גמרא begins a new defense of חזקיה, based on the scribe writing the name as two words, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A verse seems to forbid chicks whose eyes are still closed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: a פסוק about creeping things seems to include baby chicks whose eyes have not opened.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the verse comes to include chicks whose eyes have not opened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge from the previous discussion. A פסוק seems to forbid baby chicks whose eyes are still closed, which would make that a Torah-level איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim was that eating a not-yet-hatched bird does not bring מלקות. The challenge says that if a פסוק includes such chicks under the איסור of שרצים, the איסור would be מן התורה and should be fully punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: to include something extra in the law
whose eyes have not opened yet

phrases.english: To include chicks whose eyes have not opened!
phrases.notes: This finishes a challenge from before this section: a פסוק about creeping things was read as including these chicks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge begun in the previous section of the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an undeveloped bird is not forbidden on a Torah level.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק seems to include closed-eyed chicks in the איסור, which would make it a Torah-level prohibition.

steps.title: The prohibition is only rabbinic and the verse is just a support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the איסור on such chicks is only מדרבנן, and the פסוק is only a hint, called an אסמכתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is forbidden by rabbinic law, and the verse is merely a support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The איסור on these chicks comes from the רבנן, and the פסוק is only being used as a hint to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is a פסוק that the רבנן attach to their own rule, but it is not the real source of the law. So the איסור stays rabbinic, and the earlier ruling holds: there are no Torah-level מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: by rabbinic law, not from the Torah
just a support or hint, not the real source of the law

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume that every time the גמרא quotes a פסוק, the law is מן התורה. With an אסמכתא, the פסוק only 'supports' a rule the רבנן made.
steps.whatToRemember: Chicks whose eyes have not opened are forbidden only מדרבנן. The פסוק is an אסמכתא.

phrases.english: It is by rabbinic law,
and the verse is merely a support.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Downgrades the source: the פסוק is only an אסמכתא for a rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק makes closed-eyed chicks forbidden מן התורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור is only מדרבנן, so there are no Torah מלקות.

steps.title: A teaching about boiled eggs, unfertilized eggs, and a blood spot
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that boiled eggs are permitted, unfertilized eggs may be eaten by someone who isn't squeamish, and a drop of blood is thrown away while the rest is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: eggs that were boiled together are permitted. Unfertilized eggs may be eaten by a person who is not squeamish. If a drop of blood is found on an egg, he throws away the blood and eats the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with three rules about eggs. This starts a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kosher eggs boiled with non-kosher eggs are still allowed. Unfertilized eggs are allowed, but only someone with a strong stomach would want them. A small blood spot does not forbid the whole egg: you remove the blood and eat the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: eggs that were boiled, here together with non-kosher eggs
a person who is not squeamish, with a strong stomach

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Boiled eggs are permitted,
phrases.notes: He means kosher eggs that were boiled together with non-kosher ones.

phrases.english: Unfertilized eggs – a person of strong constitution may eat them,
if a drop of blood is found on it –

phrases.aramaic: זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם וְאוֹכֵל אֶת הַשְּׁאָר.
phrases.english: he throws away the blood and eats the rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about eggs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boiled eggs are permitted. Unfertilized eggs may be eaten. With a blood drop, remove the blood and eat the rest.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the base for the הלכות of blood spots in eggs.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה limits the rule to blood on the knot
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the leniency of removing the blood applies only when the blood is on the egg's 'knot'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: this is only when the blood is found on its knot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה narrows the ברייתא's leniency. You may throw away the blood and eat the rest only if the blood is on the קשר, the 'knot' of the egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sounded like any blood spot can simply be removed. רבי ירמיה adds a condition: the blood must be on the knot, the spot where a chick starts to form. Blood there shows the development has not spread elsewhere in the egg.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is only when, which adds a condition
the knot, the spot in the egg where a chick begins to develop

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
And this is when it is found on its knot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: וְהוּא שֶׁנִּמְצָא עַל קֶשֶׁר שֶׁלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the blood-drop rule in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency applies only when the blood is on the knot.

steps.title: דוסתאי's teaching: blood on the white is fine, blood on the yolk forbids the egg
steps.stepSummary: דוסתאי teaches that the leniency applies only to blood on the egg white. If the blood is on the yolk, the whole egg is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוסתאי, the father of רבי אפטוריקי, taught: they only said this when the blood is found on the white. But if it is found on the yolk, even the egg is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא from דוסתאי backs up the idea that the leniency is limited. It says where the blood may be and where it may not be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on the חלבון, the white, which is where the knot is, can be removed and the rest eaten. Blood on the חלמון, the yolk, forbids the entire egg. This matches רבי ירמיה's limit and gives the opposite case as well.

keyTerms.meaning: they only taught this in a case of, which limits a rule

phrases.english: Dostai, father of Rabbi Aptoriki, taught:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצָא עַל חֶלְבּוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ,
phrases.english: They taught this only when it is found on its white,
but if it is found on its yolk –
even the egg is forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means the rest of the egg is forbidden too, not just the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ירמיה's limit with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's limit of the leniency to blood on the knot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of דוסתאי the father of רבי אפטוריקי.

steps.title: Why does blood on the yolk forbid the whole egg?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the stricter ruling on blood in the yolk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why blood on the yolk forbids the whole egg. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With blood on the white, we only throw out the blood. The question is why the yolk should be any different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why blood on the yolk forbids the entire egg.

steps.title: Because the decay has spread through the whole egg
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that once the blood is on the yolk, the change has spread through the entire egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the decay has spread through all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason: blood on the yolk means the change has spread throughout the whole egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the white, the blood stays in one spot and can be removed. On the yolk, the תכלא, the decay or start of forming a chick, has spread everywhere, so there is no 'clean' part left to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: decay or spoilage, here the start of a chick forming

phrases.english: Because the decay has spread through all of it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood on the yolk shows the decay has spread through the whole egg.

steps.title: A version taught the opposite, and אביי fixed it
steps.stepSummary: רב גביהה tells רב אשי that a תנא once recited the ברייתא the opposite way before אביי, and אביי corrected it to the version just taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גביהה from בי כתיל said to רב אשי: a תנא recited it the opposite way before אביי, and it was אביי who corrected it for him this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב גביהה reports that a version of דוסתאי's teaching once said the reverse: yolk is fine and white is forbidden. אביי corrected it to the version we have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us the version we learned did not go unchallenged. A reciter had it backwards, and אביי fixed it so that blood on the white is allowed and blood on the yolk forbids the egg, which fits the reason about decay spreading.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter of ברייתות in the study hall

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Geviha from Bei Ketil said to Rav Ashi:
A tanna taught the opposite before Abaye,
phrases.notes: That version allowed the egg with blood on the yolk and forbade it with blood on the white.

phrases.english: and it was Abaye who corrected it for him this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב גְּבִיהָה מִבֵּי כְתִיל לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אִיפְּכָא תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the history of the wording of the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The correct version, as fixed by אביי, is that blood on the white is permitted after removal and blood on the yolk forbids the egg.
steps.whatToRemember: Blood on the white: throw out the blood and eat the rest. Blood on the yolk: the whole egg is forbidden, because the decay has spread. אביי set the wording this way.

steps.title: חזקיה's source: a non-kosher bird's egg is forbidden by the Torah
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from the words 'בת היענה' that the egg of a non-kosher bird is forbidden מן התורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: from where do we know that the egg of a non-kosher bird is forbidden by the Torah? Because it says 'and the daughter of the יענה.' Does the יענה have a daughter that needs its own mention? Rather, what is it? It is a non-kosher egg.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a Torah source for the איסור of a non-kosher bird's egg. He reads the word בת, 'daughter', as meaning its egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young of a forbidden bird would already be forbidden like its mother, so there is no need to write 'daughter.' The extra word must therefore teach something new, which is the egg.

keyTerms.meaning: the egg of a non-kosher bird
from the Torah, a Torah-level law
'the daughter of the יענה', a non-kosher bird listed in the Torah

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya says:
From where do we know that the egg of a non-kosher bird
is forbidden by Torah law?
As it is stated: "And the daughter of the ya'ana,"
But does the ya'ana have a daughter?
phrases.notes: He means a daughter that would need its own mention, since the young would be forbidden just like the mother anyway.

phrases.english: Rather, which is it? This is a non-kosher egg.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: מִנַּיִן לְבֵיצַת טְמֵאָה שֶׁהִיא אֲסוּרָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the Torah source for forbidding non-kosher eggs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-kosher bird's egg is forbidden מן התורה, learned from 'בת היענה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is חזקיה's Torah source for forbidding the egg of a non-kosher bird, and the rest of the amud tests whether the word בת can really carry that teaching.

steps.title: Maybe 'בת יענה' is simply the bird's name
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps 'בת יענה' is just the full name of the bird, and not a reference to its egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps that is their name?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's reading. Maybe the bird is simply called 'בת יענה,' so the word בת teaches nothing extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה's whole proof depends on the word בת being extra. If it is just part of the bird's name, it is not extra, and the proof about eggs falls apart.

phrases.english: But perhaps this is their name?

steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's reading of בת as the egg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'בת יענה' is the bird's full name, the word בת is not extra and cannot teach about eggs.

steps.title: A verse in איכה shows the bird is called יענה, not בת יענה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from איכה, where the bird is called 'יענים' without 'בת', so בת is not part of its name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because it is written: 'The daughter of my people has become cruel, like the יענים in the wilderness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. A פסוק in איכה calls these birds just 'יענים,' which shows that their name is יענה, without בת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the bird's own name is יענה, the word בת in the Torah really is extra. That brings back חזקיה's proof that the extra word teaches the איסור on its egg.

keyTerms.meaning: the plural of יענה, the bird

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא holds that the bird is called יענה, so 'בת' looks extra and teaches about the egg. Step 17 takes this back.

phrases.english: This should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "The daughter of my people has become cruel,
like the ye'enim in the wilderness."

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, דִּכְתִיב: ״בַּת עַמִּי לְאַכְזָר כַּיְעֵנִים בַּמִּדְבָּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and restores the proof of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proves from another פסוק that the bird's name is יענה alone, so בת is extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בת יענה' might be the bird's full name.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name is יענה, so בת teaches that the egg is forbidden.

steps.title: A verse in מיכה seems to call the bird itself 'בנות יענה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that 'בת' is not part of the bird's name. It quotes מיכה, where 'בנות יענה' are described as mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really not the bird's name? But it is written: 'I will make a wailing like the jackals, and a mourning like the בנות יענה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its last answer. It brings a פסוק where 'בנות יענה' are mourning, and only a living bird mourns, not an egg.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said 'בת' is not part of the name, because איכה calls the bird just 'יענים'. Here 'בנות יענה' are pictured as mourners, so 'בנות יענה' looks like a name for the adult bird. If so, חזקיה's proof about the egg falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'daughters of the ostrich'; the phrase being argued over
Wailing, loud crying over a loss

phrases.english: And is it not [its name]?
phrases.notes: He means: is 'בת יענה' really not a name for the bird?

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"I will make a wailing like the jackals
and a mourning like the daughters of the ostrich"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 11 that 'בת' is not part of the bird's name.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'בת יענה' is not the bird's name and so must mean its egg.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mourning is done by a living bird, so 'בנות יענה' in מיכה must be the bird itself.

steps.title: It means like the ostrich that mourns for its young
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the פסוק as a comparison: mourning like the ostrich mourns over its children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: like this ostrich that mourns over its children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'בנות' here really means the bird's children. The ostrich is the one mourning, and it mourns for its 'בנות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בנות' and 'יענה' are not one name. 'יענה' is the mother bird and 'בנות' are its young that it cries over. So the פסוק does not prove that 'בנות יענה' is the bird's name.

phrases.english: Like this ostrich
that mourns over its children.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בנות יענה' is one name for the mourning bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ostrich mourns, and 'בנות' are the young it mourns for.

steps.title: A verse in ישעיהו says 'בנות יענה' will dwell there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another פסוק where 'בנות יענה' dwell in a place, again sounding like living birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And בנות יענה shall dwell there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again with a different פסוק. Here 'בנות יענה' are living in a ruined place, which an egg cannot do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dwelling somewhere is done by a living creature. So 'בנות יענה' again seems to be the bird's name. The mourning answer of step 13 does not fit this פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that...; opens a challenge

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And the daughters of the ostrich shall dwell there"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כְּתִיב וְשָׁכְנוּ שָׁם בְּנוֹת יַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against step 11, from a different verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'בת יענה' is not the bird's name.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only living birds dwell somewhere, so 'בנות יענה' must be the bird itself.

steps.title: It means like the ostrich that dwells with its young
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא explains: the ostrich lives together with its children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: like this ostrich that dwells with its children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same kind of answer. The ostrich is the one dwelling, and 'בנות' are the young it lives with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like step 13, 'בנות' is read as the bird's young, not as part of its name. So this פסוק also does not prove that 'בנות יענה' is a name.

phrases.english: Like this ostrich
that dwells with its children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from ישעיהו 13 with the same approach as step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בנות יענה' is one name for the dwelling bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ostrich dwells, together with its young.

steps.title: An egg cannot sing praise to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a third פסוק where 'בנות יענה' honor ה׳. An egg cannot do that, and here the 'its young' answer does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'The animals of the field shall honor Me, the jackals and the בנות יענה.' If you think it means an egg, can an egg sing a song of praise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger challenge. Here 'בנות יענה' are listed with other animals that praise ה׳, so it must be a living bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק 'בנות יענה' stand on their own as a kind of animal next to the jackals. There is no mother bird doing something 'with its young', so the earlier answers do not fit. And an egg cannot praise ה׳, so 'בנות יענה' must be the bird's name.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind; if you would think
Able to say a song of praise

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is trying to answer this the same way as before. This פסוק is different because 'בנות יענה' is listed as a kind of animal on its own, so 'like the ostrich with its young' does not work.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"The animals of the field shall honor Me,
the jackals and the daughters of the ostrich",
and if it enters your mind that it means an egg,
is an egg able to say a song?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב תְּכַבְּדֵנִי חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה תַּנִּים וּבְנוֹת יַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third and stronger challenge, which the earlier style of answer cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'בת יענה' refers to the egg rather than naming the bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the bird praises ה׳. An egg cannot sing, and there is no 'mother with young' reading, so 'בנות יענה' must be the bird's name.

steps.title: Both names are used for the bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the bird is called both 'היענה' and 'בת היענה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is written 'היענה', and it is written 'בת היענה'. Both are names of the bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives in on this point. Sometimes the Torah calls the bird 'יענה' and sometimes 'בת יענה', and both are its name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes back the answer of step 11, which used איכה to show 'בת' is not part of the name. Now we see the bird has two names. So חזקיה's proof that 'בת' means the egg is in trouble, and the גמרא will have to defend him another way.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; shows the גמרא is changing its approach
The name with 'בת', also used for the bird

phrases.english: Rather, it is written "the ostrich",
and it is written "the daughter of the ostrich".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כְּתִיב הַיַּעֲנָה וּכְתִיב בַּת הַיַּעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 16 and drops the answer of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'יענה' and 'בת יענה' are both names of the bird, so the name alone does not prove 'בת' means the egg.

steps.title: The scribe writes 'בת יענה' as two words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new defense of חזקיה. This name is different because the scribe splits it into two separate words.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here it is different, because the scribe splits it into two words. And from the fact that the scribe splits them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new way to save חזקיה's proof. It points out that 'בת יענה' is written as two words, unlike other one-word animal names. The sentence continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if 'בת יענה' can be the bird's name, the way it is written is unusual. Splitting it into two words hints at something extra, and the גמרא is about to say what that teaches. This step only sets up that point.

phrases.english: But here it is different,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁאנֵי הָכָא דְּפָסֵק סָפְרָא לִשְׁתֵּי תֵּיבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After admitting both names exist, the גמרא begins a new defense of חזקיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the derivation, based on how the words are written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since 'בת יענה' is a name of the bird, חזקיה has no proof about the egg.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting the name into two words is unusual and will be used to teach about the egg (finished in the following lines).
